I assembled the lamp by rotating each part back by the angle stored in its circle arcs. I checked that rule against the bulb and shade, which come out pointing almost the same way (about 13° and 18° below horizontal). Each part was then translated so its hole lands on the matching hole of the part it joins.

Two choices could not be confirmed from the kit and are best guesses:
- **L bracket (no stored angle):** I rotated it −110° so it reads as a normal "L". The long leg with the slot becomes the foot, resting flat on the base's top edge at y = 720. The rounded leg becomes the upright, with its slot as the pin hole.
- **Head plate "hole A":** I used the lower-right hole of the two matching larger holes, so the shade hangs below the plate.

The shade's socket has no hole marker, so I placed the bulb's cap at the centre of the cone's narrow end. With that placement, part of the bulb sticks out past the shade opening.

| Part | Rotation | Joint placement |
|---|---|---|
| Base | 0° | unchanged |
| L bracket | −110° | upright pin hole ends up at (550.2, 646.9) |
| Lower arm | −35° | bottom hole on the bracket pin; top hole ends up at (338.2, 399.0) |
| Elbow plate | −125° | bottom hole on the lower arm's top hole; right hole ends up at (352.5, 334.5) |
| Upper arm | −70° | bottom hole on the elbow's right hole; top hole ends up at (593.3, 93.9) |
| Head plate | −55° | arm hole on the upper arm's top hole; hole A ends up at (654.7, 110.6) |
| Shade | −160° | lug hole on hole A; socket ends up at (670.2, 183.6) |
| Bulb | −25° | screw cap on the socket |
